summary.headline: M&M Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT up 34% and ROE at 23%, with Auto margins hit by 400-500 bps commodity inflation and Farm hit by steel and rubber.
summary.overview: Management reported consolidated PAT up 34% and revenue up 28%, with Auto PAT up 21% and Farm PAT up 15% despite 400-500 bps of Auto commodity pressure and 300+ bps in Farm. Mahindra Finance profit rose 78% on NIM recovery to 7.3% and a pivot back to growth, while Tech Mahindra profit rose 28% and Growth Gems profit rose about 3x. Auto price increases of about 2.7% on average were taken in July, and Q1 is described as the low point for Auto margins. Management stayed cautiously optimistic, and Auto management said the June commodity trend was easing while the July hedging loss of about 85 bps weighed on Q1.

financial_highlights.metric: Auto PBIT margin (core auto + LCV, ex-EV)
financial_highlights.change: down from 10.8% a year ago; trend 10.2%, 10.8%, 8.9%

financial_highlights.value: Rs 270 crore; total EV end-to-end Rs 288 crore
Rs 14 crore; business level Rs 25 crore
financial_highlights.change: highest ever quarterly profit per management

segments.name: Auto (incl. SUV, LCV, EV)
segments.commentary: SUV volume up 15% (ICE and EV together 14.9%) and LCV up 20% despite April-May production issues. EV penetration 12% vs 9% industry, with 77,000 cumulative EVs sold; EV-SUV grew 77% YoY. Auto consolidated revenue up 32%.

segments.name: Farm
segments.commentary: Volume up 18% and exports up 15%, with Farm PAT up 15%. Consolidated EBIT margin 14.2% after Erkunt Foundry impairment; EBIT growth 9% after impairment and 12% before. Steel up 24% and rubber up 30%, or 53% YTD, which cannot be hedged.

segments.name: Mahindra Finance
segments.commentary: Profit up 78%. Pivot to growth: wheels book grew about 20% and non-wheels (mortgage, SME, PL) grew 79%. GS2+GS3 has stayed below 10% for 7 quarters. Lending book about Rs 1.5 lakh crore, of which 17% non-wheels.

segments.name: Tech Mahindra
segments.commentary: Profit up 28% (and up 94% in the call's summary). EBIT margin 14.4%, with a target of 15% by end FY27.

segments.name: Growth Gems (Real Estate, Logistics, Aerospace, etc.)
segments.commentary: Combined profit up about 3x and revenue up 39%. Lifespaces added Rs 5,600 crore GDV (up 60%) and free sales of Rs 925 crore (up 2x); total GDV pipeline about Rs 50,000 crore. Logistics turned positive at Rs 14 crore at M&M level.

guidance_outlook: Auto: management expects Q1 to be the low point for margins and sees the 2.7% average price increase (plus earlier 1.5%) helping offset commodity pressure. It guided to maintaining or slightly improving Auto operating margin from Q1 to Q2 if commodities do not move sharply.

Farm: a temporary margin blip is expected because steel and rubber are unhedgeable. Q2 faces an operating leverage issue from a festival shift to 11 October, and management expects relief in Q3 from softer commodities and the season upcycle.
Group ROE target stays at 18% even though Q1 ROE was 23%; management said it is not resetting expectations.
Mahindra Finance: ROA target 2.2-2.5% (Q1 at 2.4%); non-wheels to reach 30% of book by 2031; target book of Rs 3 lakh crore by 2031.
Tech Mahindra: 15% EBIT margin target by end FY27, with a next-phase target to be announced later.

Auto capacity: ICE SUV capacity to reach 60,000 per month and EV capacity 8,000 by September, for 68,000 total; plan to reach about 92,000 by end FY28 and double capacity by FY31 via Nagpur (first phase 1H CY2029).
capex_capacity: Auto ICE SUV capacity: 60,000 per month by September 2026, plus 8,000 EV capacity, for 68,000 total capacity by September (described as ready at end of H1).
By end FY27, adds 10,000 ICE capacity for NU_IQ platform launches in FY28, and EV capacity rising from 8,000 to 12,000 for a new EV launching in FY28. Total cited as about 82,000.
Chakan adds another 10,000 per month (NU_IQ phase 2), taking capacity to about 92,000; Nagpur then adds 20,000 per month in phases, with phase 1 in 1H CY2029, for about 2x capacity by FY31.
Farm: management cited the Erkunt Foundry issue as solved and exited; impairment taken on Erkunt and one other international subsidiary.
Aerospace: order book of USD 1.2 billion cumulative, USD 600 million won in the last year; potential global acquisition under consideration.
demand_pricing: Auto: price increases of about 1.5% earlier and 2.7% average in mid-July. Management said demand has not visibly weakened from the new prices so far, and physical dealer inventory is about 15 days.
Auto: commodity pressure of 400-500 bps in Q1 (management rejected the analyst's 600-700 bps read-through); hedging loss about 85 bps QoQ. Commodity prices began rising again after June.
Tractors: channel inventory of 30-40 days, which management called fine. Shift toward 40-50 HP tractors reached about 69-70% of the mix in Q1.

Farm: management said rural sentiment is non-negative after recent rains. Kharif sowing is down just over 4% YoY, rainfall deficit about 15%, reservoirs about 7% below LPA, and government spending up 16%.
Mahindra Finance: used vehicles 15-19% of incremental disbursements over 8 quarters, with 16% last quarter. Used car ranks 2-3 and used tractor ranks 1.
Lifespaces: pricing about 15% higher than peers due to trust, and a 12,000 crore GDV joint development win. Affordable segment exited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PLI benefit in EV margins and is there a PLI 2.0 beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Shah said PLI should decline as scale lifts margins and that there is no timeline yet; clarity is expected in 6-12 months. Rajesh Jejurikar said EV is EBITDA positive without PLI, and the PLI amount was not shared.

qa_highlights.question: Tractor channel inventory and horsepower mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Channel inventory is 30-40 days, which is in line with norms, and Swaraj is below norm due to supply issues. Shift to 40-50 HP is about 69-70% of the mix in Q1, aided by implement adoption and post-GST pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Mahindra Finance is used vehicles and would the mix increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Used vehicles are 15-19% of incremental disbursements over 8 quarters; Q1 was 16% because of conservative residual value. Management expects it to return to the 16-19% range; it is margin accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity cost impact on Auto Q1 and Q2 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 commodity pressure was 400-500 bps; Anish Shah said 600-700 bps is not the right number. Hedging loss was about 85 bps. Management expects Q1 to be the low point and Auto margins to hold or improve slightly in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will EV profitability come from pricing or cost, and when is the inflection?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Jejurikar said both levers; EV penetration inflection expected at 20-25%, with a 5-7% premium possible after that. Cost curve benefits expected within 12-18 months. Dr. Shah said Auto margins can reach ICE levels over time with scale.

qa_highlights.question: Lifespaces five-year vision and fit in the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Target pre-sales of Rs 10,000 crore by FY30 (14x FY20), focused on Mumbai, Pune and Bangalore (about 55% of national unit sales), premium and mid-premium segments. Group fit depends on quality, scale and profitability/ROA.

qa_highlights.question: Mahindra Finance diversification and ROA path?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-wheels is 17% of the Rs 1.5 lakh crore book. Target 70:30 mobility to non-wheels by 2031 and Rs 3 lakh crore book. ROA target 2.2-2.5%, with 2.4% in Q1.

risks_watch: Auto commodity pressure: Q1 hit of 400-500 bps with June trend easing but commodity prices rising again after June; management declined to bake in the hedging MTM, which was a QoQ loss of about 85 bps and is highly volatile

Auto supply and production: July lost about 3 days to rain and flooding, plus a fire at a large southern supplier; physical dealer inventory about 15 days; capacity ramp to 68,000 by September depends on supplier commitments

Farm margin blip: steel up 24% and rubber up 30% (53% YTD), both unhedgeable; Q2 has operating leverage pressure from festival shifting to 11 October; Kharif sowing about 4% below last year, rainfall deficit about 15%
Auto price increases of about 1.5% and 2.7% average taken mid-July: watch whether demand holds and whether further price moves are needed before the festive season
EV profitability depends on PLI, which management said will reduce as margins rise, with no timeline; clarity expected in 6-12 months; EV penetration inflection expected at 20-25%

Mahindra Finance: sustaining NIM recovery (7.3%) and ROA (2.4% vs 2.2-2.5% target) while growing non-wheels (17% of the Rs 1.5 lakh crore book) and used vehicles (16% of incremental disbursements last quarter)
key_quotes: So, we are not resetting expectations, we will stay with 18% as a target there.
Overall, I would say, that we are on balance cautiously optimistic as well.
So, I wouldn't get to 600 -700. I think 400 -500 is what we saw in Q1, for most of Q1.
And that's the reason why we say we feel good about the future in that sense.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic overall, with management describing Q1 as the low point for Auto margins and expecting maintenance or slight improvement in Q2 if commodities do not move sharply. Management was more guarded on Farm, flagging a temporary margin blip from unhedgeable steel and rubber and a Q2 festival-shift effect, and declined to share PLI amounts, used-vehicle pricing or demand-enquiry detail.
